### Will Graham Devotion: Solomon's Secret Weapon
Author: Will Graham
Site: Billy Graham Evangelistic Association
URL: https://billygraham.org/articles/will-graham-devotion-what-does-true-wisdom-look-like?ri=wc
Passage: 2 Chronicles 1:1-15
Points:
- Solomon began his reign not by indulging in royal entitlement, but by leading the entire nation in worship before God.
- Following Solomon's sacrifice at Gibeon, God appeared and granted him an open invitation to make any request.
- Conscious of his own inadequacy to govern God's chosen people, Solomon requested wisdom and knowledge rather than wealth or vengeance.
- Pleased by Solomon's selfless heart, God gave him unprecedented wisdom along with honor, riches, and influence.
- Believers in every position of life are called to humble themselves, place worship first, and rely completely on God's guidance.

### Wisdom, Knowledge, Service: Take Your Place in the Kingdom of God
Author: T.M. Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/spiritual-life/wisdom-knowledge-service-take-your-place-in-the-kingdom-of-god-11559624.html
Passage: 2 Chronicles 1:10
Points:
- Solomon felt overwhelmed by his calling to rule Israel, leading him to ask God for wisdom and knowledge.
- Genuine knowledge requires viewing creation from God's heavenly perspective rather than from an earthbound viewpoint.
- True knowledge is necessarily incomplete in this life and must be continually deepened through scripture and the Holy Spirit.
- Wisdom is the practical fruit of knowledge, demonstrating itself through love for God, love for neighbor, and righteous living.
- Solomon's desire was selfless, showing that spiritual knowledge and wisdom exist to equip believers to serve others.

### A New Perspective on King Solomon - Warrior Mom Wisdom - Week of July 2
Author: Kristina Seymour
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/warrior-mom-wisdom/warrior-mom-wisdom-week-of-february-6.html
Passage: 2 Chronicles 1:11-12
Points:
- People rarely ask for things they already possess, and Solomon had already inherited enormous wealth and security from David.
- Solomon recognized that the people belonged to the Lord, causing him to ask for the discernment needed to lead them well.
- Receiving an inheritance without personal struggle carries the danger of taking its high cost for granted.
- In the same way Solomon inherited a kingdom without shedding blood, Christians inherit eternal life through Christ's sacrifice.
- Believers must guard against spiritual apathy and live in daily gratitude for what Jesus purchased on the cross.

### Bible Pathways 05/21/2002
Author: Bible Pathways Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-05-or-21-or-2002-1133446.html
Passage: 2 Chronicles 1:3
Points:
- Solomon opened his reign in submission to the Lord, assembling the leaders of Israel to seek God at the Tabernacle in Gibeon.
- When the Lord appeared to him in a dream, Solomon rightly recognized that his greatest need was divine wisdom to guide God's people.
- Although Solomon began well, he eventually allowed personal ambition and worldly alliances to override God's clear commands.
- Solomon's later spiritual decline serves as a solemn warning to maintain consistent, lifelong obedience to God's Word.
- Earthly renown and material prosperity are meaningless compared to allowing God to direct our hearts and abilities.
